battle.name: 西班牙再征服墨西哥
battle.brief: 一八二一年七月起，西班牙王室不承認《科爾多瓦條約》，企圖以遠征隊重奪新西班牙；三保軍入墨之後，米納一八二七年自西班牙渡海，在墨西哥灣岸的塔姆皮科登陸，翌年兵敗被俘。輪發手槍是西班牙軍官與近衛的舊制手槍，此時早已讓位於燧發槍，象徵這場再征服只靠小規模遠征隊與個人火器撐起。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 交戰的一方是西班牙王國及其美洲殖民體系。一八二一年墨西哥宣布獨立時，總督胡安·德·奧多諾胡所掌握的西班牙海軍分遣隊與駐軍，仍控制維拉克魯斯港、墨西哥城內的要塞與數處沿海據點；一八二二年起，馬德里的斐迪南七世王廷以《科爾多瓦條約》未經批准為由，拒絕承認墨西哥的獨立，並利用墨西哥境內的保皇派作為內應，陸續在古巴與本土策劃遠征。另一方是新生不久的墨西哥：一八二一年九月至一八二三年的墨西哥帝國與其「三保軍」，一八二四年之後的聯邦共和國，以及新萊昂、科阿韋拉、塔毛利帕斯等邊疆州的聯邦軍與民兵。西班牙流亡自由派則構成第三股力量：法國波旁王朝以「十萬聖路易之子」干涉西班牙所造成的大批流亡，催生了以弗朗西斯科·哈維爾·米納為首的一八二七年遠征隊，隊伍中夾有英國、法國的志願者與冒險家。列強並未公開參戰：英國港口為遠征隊提供船隻與軍火，美國因《亞當斯—奧尼斯條約》劃定的邊界以及得克薩斯殖民問題而高度關注，同一時期德克薩斯的弗雷多尼亞叛亂亦牽動墨西哥北部邊疆的部署。
countriesEn: One side of the conflict was the Crown of Spain together with its American colonial apparatus. When Mexico proclaimed its independence in 1821, the Spanish naval squadron and garrison under Viceroy Juan de O'Donojú still held the port of Veracruz, the citadels inside Mexico City and a number of coastal strongholds; from 1822 the court of Ferdinand VII in Madrid, on the ground that the Treaty of Córdoba had never been ratified, refused to recognise Mexican independence and employed the pro-Spanish royalist factions inside Mexico as agents, planning expeditions from Cuba and from the peninsula. The other side was the new Mexican state: the First Mexican Empire and its Army of the Three Guarantees from September 1821 to 1823, the Federal Republic after 1824, and the federal regulars and militias of the border states of Nuevo León, Coahuila and Tamaulipas. Spanish liberal exiles formed a third force, for the mass exile produced by the Bourbon intervention in Spain under the banner of the Hundred Thousand Sons of Saint Louis produced the 1827 expedition led by Francisco Xavier Mina, with British and French volunteers and adventurers mixed into its ranks. The great powers did not join openly: British ports supplied the expedition with shipping and munitions, while the United States watched closely because of the border drawn by the Adams-Onis Treaty and the question of the Texas colony, and the Fredonian rebellion in Texas in the same years disturbed Mexico's deployments on her northern frontier.
people: 關鍵人物分屬三邊。西班牙方面，總督胡安·德·奧多諾胡是《科爾多瓦條約》的西班牙代表，瓜達拉哈拉都督卡洛斯·德·拉·佩德拉達共同簽署；一八二一年九月，最後一批西班牙軍隊與海軍駛離墨西哥，奧多諾胡其後被召回本土。古巴都督弗朗西斯科·達維拉在一八二九年於哈瓦那組裝遠征船隊，最後被迫取消。流亡自由派領袖弗朗西斯科·哈維爾·米納是整場再征服企圖中最具行動力的角色：他在加的斯登船後率數百人渡海，一八二七年底在墨西哥東北部登陸，隨即被新聖安塔內里奧省長米格爾·巴爾巴查諾的聯邦軍擊敗，一八二八年被俘並在維拉克魯斯槍決。墨西哥方面，阿古斯丁·德·伊圖爾維德是關鍵：這位前西班牙皇家陸軍中尉以《伊瓜拉方案》起家，率領「三保軍」，並於一八二一年二月十日在阿卡特姆潘與維森特·格雷羅握手，翌年加冕為皇帝，一八二三年退位離境；聯邦軍將領曼努埃爾·米爾·伊·特蘭在北部戰線擊敗米納，隨後率軍北上，於一八三八年遠征得州。
peopleEn: The decisive figures belong to three different camps. On the Spanish side, Viceroy Juan de O'Donojú was the Spanish signatory of the Treaty of Córdoba, together with Captain General of Guatemala Carlos de la Pedrada; in September 1821 the last Spanish troops and warships left Mexico, and O'Donojú was later recalled to the peninsula. Francisco Dávila, Captain General of Cuba, assembled an expeditionary fleet at Havana in 1829 and was ultimately forced to cancel it. The leader of the liberal exiles, Francisco Xavier Mina, was the most active figure in the whole reconquest effort: he embarked at Cádiz and crossed the Atlantic with several hundred men, landing on the north-eastern coast of Mexico at the end of 1827, only to be beaten by the federal forces of Miguel Barbachano, governor of Nuevo Santander, captured in 1828 and shot at Veracruz. On the Mexican side the key figure was Agustín de Iturbide, a former lieutenant of the Spanish royal army who started the movement with the Plan of Iguala, led the Army of the Three Guarantees, and on 10 February 1821 shook hands with Vicente Guerrero at Acatempan; crowned the following year, he abdicated and left the country in 1823. The federal commander Manuel Mier y Terán defeated Mina on the northern front and later led his army north in the expedition against Texas in 1838.
kits: 卡面這件輪發手槍，是十五世紀末至十六世紀初出現的後膛手槍，機括靠扳機拉動釋放掣子，帶動擊錘撞擊燧石，火星落入火藥盤，是人類最早可以單手重複擊發的後膛火器。但它零件多、造價高，一直只有西班牙王室的近衛軍與各級軍官配發，士卒仍用火繩槍與長矛。到一八二一年，真實的西班牙軍隊早已全面換用燧發槍：步兵是米奎萊特式燧發滑膛槍，軍官與士官是佩德雷里爾式燧發手槍，只有王室儀仗、宮廷衛隊以及老將軍的隨身佩槍中才仍見輪發手槍。因此在墨西哥戰線上，輪發手槍的位置早已不是主力火器，而是「軍官身分」本身——它代表指揮權與傳統，也代表一支缺乏重裝備的遠征小分隊仍能倚仗的近身自衛火力。同場出現的裝備還包括維拉克魯斯與墨西哥城兵工廠出產的西班牙式燧發火槍、老式火繩槍、義大利式滑鐵加簧燧發手槍、騎兵用的燧發卡賓槍、鑄鐵滑膛野戰炮與護航分遣隊所配的十二磅以上艦炮，以及三保軍自聖路易波托西與普埃布拉運來的彈藥車、火藥與攻城器材。
kitsEn: The wheellock pistol on the card face first appeared in the late fifteenth and early sixteenth century. Its mechanism is released by pulling the trigger, which frees a sear and drives the hammer against the pyrite, showering sparks into the priming pan; it is the earliest breech-loading firearm that a single hand could fire repeatedly. But the mechanism had many parts and was expensive, so it was issued only to the royal guard and to officers, while rank and file still carried matchlock muskets and pikes. By 1821 the real Spanish army had moved entirely to flintlock: miquelet flintlock smoothbore muskets for the infantry, pedreril flintlock pistols for officers and non-commissioned officers, and wheellocks surviving only in royal pageantry, the household guard and the personal arms of old generals. On the Mexican front, therefore, the wheellock no longer belonged to the order of battle as a main weapon; it stood for the officer corps itself, for command and tradition, and for the close-quarter personal fire a small expeditionary column without heavy equipment still relied on. The rest of the equipment present in the same theatre included Spanish-pattern flintlock muskets from the arsenals of Veracruz and Mexico City, old matchlocks, Italian possibles flintlock pistols, flintlock carbines for cavalry, cast-iron smoothbore field guns, twelve-pounder and heavier naval guns carried by the escort squadrons, and the ammunition wagons, gunpowder and siege material brought up by the Army of the Three Guarantees from San Luis Potosí and Puebla.
tactics: 一八二一年三保軍入城靠的不是攻城，而是行軍：一支輕裝縱隊沿維拉克魯斯、哈利斯科、普埃布拉至墨西哥城的皇家道路北上，砲車、彈藥車與給養車隊沿同一條路跟進，隊伍之間以縱隊相隔固定距離，避免高山隘口與雨季道路把行軍縱列拉斷。同時，墨西哥城約八公里的城牆在獨立之後被主動拆成通衢，拆下的石料用來拓寬大道，後來被稱為改革大道——城牆自己消失，意味著任何遠征縱隊不必先攻要塞便可直入城中，這對西班牙的再征服企圖既是便利，也是不祥。一八二二年至一八二三年的帝國與共和派內戰裡，雙方都沿上述幹線對進：帝國軍在哈利斯科的哈利阿特拉科橋一役（一八二三年一月六日）擊敗共和派，隨後圍困普埃布拉、瓦哈卡與塔曼比亞的據點；共和派則退入南部山區，改以游擊與迂迴斷糧。米納的遠征隊採取另一套打法：船隊在墨西哥灣登陸之後不直取墨西哥城，而是沿塔毛利帕斯內陸向普埃布洛維耶霍（今日塔毛利帕斯州維多利亞城）推進，企圖以小型遠征隊配合當地起義者製造內亂；聯邦軍則以主力正面封鎖、以民兵與騎兵切斷退路，最終在切德爾一役把遠征隊耗盡。
tacticsEn: The Army of the Three Guarantees entered Mexico City in 1821 not by siege but by marching: a lightly equipped column moved north along the royal road running from Veracruz through Xalapa and Puebla to Mexico City, with the gun teams, ammunition wagons and supply train following the same track, columns kept at fixed intervals so that mountain passes and rainy-season roads could not stretch the marching order apart. At the same time the roughly eight kilometres of Mexico City's walls were deliberately demolished after independence, the stone reused to widen the great avenue later called the Paseo de la Reforma; the walls had removed themselves, which meant that an invading column need not reduce a single fortress before entering the city, a convenience for the Spanish reconquest and an ill omen as well. During the civil war between the Empire and the republicans from 1822 to 1823 both sides moved against each other along the same arteries: the imperial army beat the republicans at the Puente de Jalatlaco near Xalapa on 6 January 1823 and then besieged Puebla, Oaxaca and the strongholds of Tamazula; the republicans withdrew into the southern mountains and switched to harrying the lines and cutting supplies. Mina's expedition tried yet another method: after landing on the Gulf coast it did not strike for Mexico City but pushed inland through Tamaulipas toward Pueblo Viejo, the modern Ciudad Victoria, hoping that a small expeditionary column joined by local insurgents would stir up a general insurrection. The federal army answered by sealing the approaches with regular columns, cutting the retreat with militia and cavalry, and finally wore the expedition down in the action at Cedral.
data: 可核對的數字以日期為主。一八一○年九月「獨立第一聲」響起，到一八二一年九月《墨西哥帝國獨立宣言》簽署，戰爭打了十一年。一八二一年二月十日阿卡特姆潘會晤，八月二十四日《科爾多瓦條約》簽訂，九月二十七日三保軍進入墨西哥城。首任墨西哥帝國皇帝伊圖爾維德於一八二二年七月加冕，翌年七月十九日退位，二十七日由維拉克魯斯登船離境，次年七月十九日在墨西哥城被處決。聯邦共和國於一八二六年獲美國承認，隨後又與英國達成商務條約。遠征方面，米納於一八二五年秋自西班牙桑坦德出航，率約二百人渡大西洋，航程七千五百公里上下；一八二七年十一月底在墨西哥東北部登陸，次年一月在切德爾一役覆沒，六月被俘，七月在維拉克魯斯槍決。一八二九年古巴都督達維拉在哈瓦那集結的遠征隊規模約一千五百至二千人，卻在出航前被叫停。同年六月霍亂疫情傳入墨西哥城，軍方在一八二九年二月的聖十字營事件中幾乎失去對民兵的控制。關於西班牙守軍撤離時的具體人數，各史料說法由數百至數千不等，諸說並存。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are mostly dates. From the first cry of independence in September 1810 to the signing of the Declaration of Independence of the Mexican Empire in September 1821 the war had run for eleven years. The Acatempan meeting was on 10 February 1821, the Treaty of Córdoba was signed on 24 August, and the Army of the Three Guarantees entered Mexico City on 27 September. Agustín de Iturbide, the first and only Mexican emperor, was crowned in July 1822, abdicated on 19 July 1823, sailed from Veracruz on the twenty-seventh, and was executed in Mexico City on 19 July of the following year. The Federal Republic was recognised by the United States in 1826 and later concluded a commercial treaty with Britain. On the expedition side, Mina sailed from Santander in Spain in the autumn of 1825 with some two hundred men, crossing roughly seven and a half thousand kilometres of the Atlantic; he landed on the north-eastern coast of Mexico at the end of November 1827, was destroyed at Cedral in January 1828, captured in June and shot at Veracruz in July. The expedition Francisco Dávila assembled at Havana in 1829 numbered roughly one thousand five hundred to two thousand men and was called off before it sailed. The same year, in June, cholera reached Mexico City, and the army very nearly lost control of the militia during the Campo de Santa Cruz affair in February 1829. The precise number of Spanish troops who departed in the withdrawal is given differently in different sources, ranging from several hundred to several thousand, and the figures stand as they are.
cause: 再征服的第一層原因是法理與王權：斐迪南七世的波旁王廷把一八二○年自由革命後形成的《科爾多瓦條約》視為地方總督越權的產物，認為墨西哥的獨立必須經母國議會批准方能生效，於是拒絕承認。第二層原因是西班牙本土的政治擠壓：一八二三年法國波旁王朝以「十萬聖路易之子」干涉西班牙，鎮壓自由派、恢復專制，大批自由派軍官流亡英國與法國，其中米納最積極地籌劃武裝回國。第三層原因是墨西哥自身的不穩定：帝國與共和派的內戰讓保皇派與西班牙方面都相信有機可乘，保守派軍閥如新聖安塔內里奧省長巴爾巴查諾在北部邊疆的嚴酷治理，也讓流亡者相信可以就地號召。第四層原因是帝國崩潰留下的真空：一八二三年退位的伊圖爾維德在歐洲流亡，其帝國軍與支持者仍願意為西班牙所用，而聯邦政府尚未在北部邊疆建立有效而穩定的指揮體系。
causeEn: The first cause of the reconquest was one of legality and royal prerogative: the Bourbon court of Ferdinand VII treated the Treaty of Córdoba, signed after the liberal revolution of 1820, as the overreach of a colonial viceroy, and held that Mexican independence could only be valid once approved by the Cortes in the mother country. The second cause was the political pressure at home in Spain: in 1823 the Bourbon monarchy in France intervened with the Hundred Thousand Sons of Saint Louis, crushing the liberals and restoring absolutism, and large numbers of liberal officers went into exile in Britain and France, Mina among them being the most active in planning an armed return. The third cause was Mexico's own instability: the civil war between Empire and republicans convinced both the royalists inside Mexico and Spain that an opening existed, and the harsh government of conservative military governors such as Miguel Barbachano in Nuevo Santander persuaded the exiles that they could raise a rising on the spot. The fourth cause was the vacuum left by the collapse of the Empire: Iturbide, who abdicated in 1823, was in exile in Europe, and his imperial troops and partisans remained willing to be used by Spain, while the federal government had not yet built an effective and stable command structure on the northern frontier.
impact: 再征服的失敗，在墨西哥與西班牙兩邊都留下長期後果。對墨西哥而言，聯邦軍在北部擊敗米納、其後又在得州邊境擊退法國支持的聖安納派遠征（一八三八年），並捱過一八三八年至一八三九年的糕餅戰爭，這些戰鬥把新生的聯邦軍鍛造成一支能打遠征戰與邊疆戰的正規軍，也讓得克薩斯問題與加利福尼亞問題成為西班牙無法利用的缺口。更深一層的意義在西班牙流亡社群：米納與一批志願者的失敗，成為歐洲自由派論證小型遠征不足以改變殖民地局勢的具體案例，也為西班牙本國的專制政權添上一項「母國在海外落敗」的教訓。對歐洲而言，墨西哥守住獨立，成為美國在美洲擴張時一個不受干預的示範；而英國在墨西哥的商貿利益與法國對西班牙的牽制，則共同決定了列強沒有公然介入這場再征服。
impactEn: The failure of the reconquest left long-term consequences on both sides. For Mexico, the federal defeat of Mina in the north, the repulse of Santa Anna's French-backed expedition on the Texan border in 1838, and the war of 1838 to 1839 that followed the pastry incident turned a newborn federal army into a regular force able to fight distant expeditions and frontier wars, and turned the questions of Texas and California into gaps Spain could never exploit. Deeper still was the meaning for the Spanish exiles: the ruin of Mina and his volunteers became a concrete demonstration, for European liberals, that a small expedition could not reverse the course of a colony, and it added a lesson in defeat overseas to the repertory of the Spanish absolutist regime at home. For Europe, Mexico's successful defence of its independence became a precedent of a sovereign state untouched by interference as the United States expanded in the hemisphere, and British commercial interests in Mexico together with French leverage over Spain decided that the great powers would not openly enter this reconquest.
result: 結果是西班牙在一八二一年至一八二九年之間的三次企圖全部落空。第一階段以撤軍告終：最後一批西班牙軍隊與海軍於一八二一年九月離開維拉克魯斯與墨西哥城，墨西哥城要塞移交三保軍，墨西哥在事實上取得獨立。第二階段以帝國崩潰告終：一八二三年共和派在普埃布拉、瓦哈卡與南部海岸收復多城，伊圖爾維德退位赴歐，皇室的墨西哥方案隨之瓦解。第三階段以遠征隊覆沒告終：米納於一八二八年被墨西哥聯邦軍俘虜並槍決，其攜帶的武器與人員大多散入地方；一八二九年達維拉在哈瓦那組成的遠征隊因軍中疫情、地方反抗與哈瓦那的變亂而被取消。西班牙直到一八四○年代才在對外條約中正式承認墨西哥的獨立，這場長達八年的「再征服」最終以墨西哥完全獨立、西班牙放棄美洲殖民戰略而收場。
resultEn: In the end all three Spanish attempts between 1821 and 1829 failed. The first phase ended in a withdrawal: the last Spanish troops and warships left Veracruz and Mexico City in September 1821, the citadels of the capital passed to the Army of the Three Guarantees, and Mexico obtained its independence in fact. The second phase ended in the collapse of the Empire: in 1823 the republicans retook Puebla, Oaxaca and towns along the southern coast, Iturbide abdicated and sailed for Europe, and the royalist scheme for a dependent Mexico fell apart with him. The third phase ended in the destruction of an expeditionary force: Mina was taken prisoner by the Mexican federal army in 1828 and shot, and the weapons and men he had brought scattered into the provinces; the expedition Dávila assembled at Havana in 1829 was cancelled because of sickness in the troops, local resistance and the disorders in Havana itself. Spain did not formally acknowledge Mexican independence in its treaties until the 1840s, and this eight-year reconquest therefore closed with a fully independent Mexico and the abandonment by Spain of any colonial strategy in the Americas.
